LESSON: ATHLETICS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: PERFORMING AND DISPLAYING Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested
Topic 2.1: Athletics

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Athletics. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to maintain appropriate posture during sprints?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques in athletics
2. perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development
3. recognise the value of flying the Kenyan flag during an athletics event

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ATHLETICS
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Athletics helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ATHLETICS
Study Athletics like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques in athletics

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques in athletics. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques in athletics.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Athletics” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques in athletics. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development

What this means
In this part you learn to perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Athletics in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recognise the value of flying the Kenyan flag during an athletics event

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the value of flying the Kenyan flag during an athletics event. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the value of flying the Kenyan flag during an athletics event.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the value of flying the Kenyan flag during an athletics event. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Athletics is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Athletics” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques in athletics)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Athletics in your own words. (skill: perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: recognise the value of flying the Kenyan flag during an athletics event)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Athletics to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques in athletics.
3. Practise this skill: perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development.
4. Practise this skill: recognise the value of flying the Kenyan flag during an athletics event.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Athletics from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Athletics: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Athletics?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to maintain appropriate posture during sprints?
2. Why is the national flag flown during a national athletic event?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Athletics means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques in athletics.
5. Be able to: perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
